bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : CM Samrat Choudhary urges assistant professors to ensure 75% attendance in colleges
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar: CM Samrat Choudhary urges assistant professors to ensure 75% attendance in colleges ANI | Updated: Sep 13, 2026 13:40 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 13 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday urged newly appointed assistant professors to ensure at least 75 per cent attendance of students in colleges, saying the government's efforts to expand higher education would not yield results if students did not attend classes regularly. Addressing a gathering of newly appointed assistant professors, CM Choudhary said the state government had opened 211 degree colleges and appointed 2,451 assistant professors, describing the expansion of higher education infrastructure as a major achievement. He said the newly appointed teachers would play a key role in strengthening the academic ecosystem of the new colleges, particularly those located in rural areas and ensuring that students make full use of the facilities being created by the government. "Until children come and study in your colleges, the importance of that college will not be realised. Ensure that 75 per cent of students attend your college under all circumstances so that you can teach them," CM Choudhary said. He said students from Bihar were still travelling to cities such as Kota, Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru for higher education and competitive examination preparation. Citing examples of students studying outside the state, the Chief Minister said around 11,000 students from Bihar were studying at Lovely Professional University, while another institute in had more than 40,000 students from Bihar . "Today, around 8 to 10 lakh children from Bihar are still going outside the state to study," he said, adding that the expansion of degree colleges would provide students an opportunity to pursue higher education closer to their homes. CM Choudhary also said the government would identify 10 good international institutions and facilitate direct interaction between Bihar 's teachers and those institutions. He suggested that 100 teachers be identified and sent abroad for one-month courses to expose them to international standards of education. "One era saw us compromise quality with quantity. Now we have to take quality and quantity together," he said. The Chief Minister said the government would build college infrastructure, but the future of the institutions would depend on teachers and their efforts to improve the quality of education. He said Bihar spends more than 21 per cent of its budget in the education sector, covering primary schools, middle schools, high schools and colleges. CM Choudhary also highlighted the government's efforts to reduce the need for students to travel outside Bihar for education and said the state must compete with private universities by becoming a partner in building the future of its students. "Once Bihar picks up speed, we believe Bihar will return to the world map because history belongs to us," he said. He urged the newly appointed assistant professors to work towards changing Bihar 's education system and shaping the future of the students who would study in the 211 new degree colleges. (ANI)

national_raw_news.content: BRICS leaders have condemned the April 2025 Pahalgam terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir. In a joint statement, BRICS leaders have called for zero tolerance towards terrorism, reaffirming the regional bloc’s commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms. The New Delhi Declaration, adopted unanimously on the opening day of the summit, said that all acts of terrorism are criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation and who committed such an act. Akashvani correspondent reports that the New Delhi declaration condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April 2025, during which 26 people were killed and many more injured. The attack was later traced to terrorists backed and trained in Pakistan. The declaration also called for action against the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing, and safe havens. BRICS leaders also urged the member nations to ensure zero tolerance for terrorism and reject double standards in countering terrorism. They further called for concerted actions against all UN-designated terrorists and terrorist entities. The joint declaration also expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for maximum restraint and for avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation. It said the BRICS countries will increase efforts, through dialogue and diplomacy, towards a long-term understanding that will contribute to lasting peace, security and stability in the region. BRICS leaders also stressed the need to work together to maintain a smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law. The BRICS bloc expressed concern about the ongoing conflicts in many parts of the world and the current state of polarisation and fragmentation in the international order.

national_raw_news.content: Today is the second and final day of the BRICS summit. Today BRICS Member and Partner Countries will participate in the session based on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth. The ten partner countries are Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam. After the conclusion of the session, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold bilateral meetings with Presidents of Kazakhstan, Philippines, Egypt, South Africa and Burundi. He will also hold meetings with Vice Presidents of Nigeria and Uganda. The Summit is being held under India’s BRICS chairship, with the theme, Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. With BRICS team, Anand Kumar, Akashvani News Delhi. The two-day summit began yesterday at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The BRICS nations adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026 on the first day of the Summit itself. The BRICS nations reiterated their commitment to the peaceful resolution of international disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy. The leaders also expressed their concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation. They also strongly condemned the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April last year in the strongest terms and reaffirmed their commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. India is organising the Summit for the fourth time.

national_raw_news.content: Significance of interdisciplinary, evidence-based research in Ayurveda highlighted at Jamnagar workshop Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Significance of interdisciplinary, evidence-based research in Ayurveda highlighted at Jamnagar workshop ANI | Updated: Sep 13, 2026 08:34 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 13 (ANI): The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Ayush, organised a three-day intensive workshop which highlighted the importance of interdisciplinary and evidence-based research for generating scientifically validated knowledge and strengthening the scientific foundation of Ayurveda . The workshop, ‘Understanding Health and Wellness through Microbiome Research ’ held from September 9 to 11, aimed to familiarise participants with emerging developments in microbiome research and explore its potential relevance to health, wellness and preventive healthcare from an Ayurvedic perspective, according to the release. Prof. Sharmila Mande, Ayush Distinguished Scientist Chair, Ministry of Ayush, and Dr. Tarini Shankar Ghosh, Assistant Professor, IIIT-Delhi, delivered sessions during the workshop and shared insights into contemporary concepts, research methodologies and emerging evidence in microbiome science. The interactions provided participants with an opportunity to understand the potential implications of microbiome research for human health. The workshop brought together Ayurvedic knowledge and contemporary microbiome science, with discussions covering areas including diet, digestion, metabolism, health promotion and individualised approaches to health and wellness. The workshop concluded with a brainstorming session led by Prof. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, to identify potential areas for collaborative and multi-centric research. Discussions explored the scientific investigation of Ayurvedic concepts such as Agni (digestion and metabolism), Ahara (diet), Prakriti, healthy lifestyle practices and Ayurvedic therapies in relation to gut microbial communities. A total of 52 faculty members and research scholars participated in the three-day workshop. The programme facilitated knowledge exchange, scientific dialogue and identification of future avenues for collaborative research. The initiative is expected to contribute to strengthening interdisciplinary research at the interface of Ayurveda and modern scientific disciplines. Microbiome research offers potential avenues for studying traditional Ayurvedic concepts through contemporary scientific frameworks and developing evidence-based approaches in areas such as preventive healthcare, nutrition, digestive health, metabolic health and overall wellness. The workshop is part of ITRA’s continued efforts to promote evidence-based, interdisciplinary and public-health-oriented research in Ayurveda , with the objective of translating traditional knowledge into scientifically validated approaches for promoting health and well-being. Among the proposals outlined by Dalela was the BRICS Troika mechanism, an arrangement intended to ensure greater continuity and coordination in the bloc’s leadership transitions between the outgoing, current and incoming chairs of the grouping. Modi also proposed a roadmap for reforming global governance structures, a theme that has featured prominently in India’s engagement with multilateral institutions in recent years as emerging economies push for a greater voice in bodies that were largely shaped in the aftermath of the Second World War. The Prime Minister’s proposals additionally included assistance measures for seafarers stranded in crisis situations, an issue that has drawn increasing international attention amid conflicts and geopolitical disruptions affecting global shipping routes, along with measures aimed at enhancing the negotiating capacity of the Global South, a grouping of developing nations that BRICS has increasingly positioned itself as a voice for on the world stage. Dalela’s briefing offered one of the clearest official summaries yet of the substantive agenda India has pushed during its chairship of the bloc this year, with the initiatives spanning institutional reform, economic cooperation and humanitarian concerns. A 13 member delegation comprising journalists from Srinagar along with PIB officials will take part in the tour. Ahead of the delegation’s departure, Director PIB Srinagar, Qazi Salman, briefed the participants on the objectives of the visit, urging them to make meaningful use of the interactions and interviews planned during their time in Chennai. The delegation is being led by Shahid Lone, Field Publicity Officer at CBC Anantnag, who will serve as Conducting Officer for the tour, with Ifham Ul Islam, Information Assistant at PIB Srinagar, also accompanying the group. The tour is designed to give the visiting journalists firsthand exposure to key Central Government institutions, projects and initiatives based in Chennai, with the aim of deepening their understanding of national level policies and how these are implemented on the ground in different parts of the country. During the visit, the delegation will tour various Central Government establishments and projects in the city and interact with senior officials to better understand their functioning and day to day operations. Addressing the delegation before departure, Qazi Salman congratulated the participants and expressed confidence that the visit would offer valuable opportunities for professional engagement and a better understanding of how Central Government institutions function beyond what journalists typically encounter in their regular regional coverage. national_raw_news.content: BRICS Summit Spotlights Dravidian Architecture - https://onlykashmir.in/ Facebook Instagram Pinterest X Website Youtube State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Only Kashmir Behind The News Facebook Instagram X Only Kashmir Behind The News State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Home National National Spotlight BRICS Summit Spotlights Dravidian Architecture By Online Editor September 12, 2026 Advertisement Mirwaiz Umar Farooq meets Iranian President and Foreign Minister in New Delhi September 13, 2026 J&K Filmmakers Win Big at IFFJK 2026 September 12, 2026 PIB Srinagar Takes Journalists on Chennai Tour September 12, 2026 J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects September 12, 2026 PM Modi Pitches Key BRICS Initiatives September 12, 2026 Advertisement - Advertisement - Onlykashmir.in News Desk The 18th BRICS Summit offered visiting world leaders a striking glimpse of South India’s architectural heritage, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcoming delegations at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi against the backdrop of a grand corridor replicating the Rameswaram temple, built in the distinctive Dravidian architectural style. Tamil Nadu’s celebrated Ramanathaswamy Temple, on which the showcased corridor draws its design inspiration, is one of the four sites that make up the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit and is dedicated to Devadidev Mahadev, making its presence at a gathering of major world leaders a deliberate nod to one of South India’s most revered religious and architectural landmarks. The choice echoes a pattern Modi has followed at previous major international gatherings hosted by India. During the G20 Summit held in New Delhi in 2023, the Prime Minister had similarly used the venue’s design to introduce visiting leaders to the architectural artistry of the Konark Temple in Odisha, using India’s presidency of major multilateral forums as an occasion to showcase the country’s diverse regional heritage to a global audience. The Rameswaram corridor at this year’s BRICS Summit continues that pattern, offering the visiting leaders from all eleven BRICS member nations a visual introduction to South India’s temple architecture even as substantive discussions on economic and strategic cooperation unfolded around them. national_raw_news.content: J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects - https://onlykashmir.in/ Facebook Instagram Pinterest X Website Youtube State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Only Kashmir Behind The News Facebook Instagram X Only Kashmir Behind The News State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Home Spotlight Spotlight State J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects By Online Editor September 12, 2026 Advertisement Mirwaiz Umar Farooq meets Iranian President and Foreign Minister in New Delhi September 13, 2026 J&K Filmmakers Win Big at IFFJK 2026 September 12, 2026 PIB Srinagar Takes Journalists on Chennai Tour September 12, 2026 J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects September 12, 2026 PM Modi Pitches Key BRICS Initiatives September 12, 2026 Advertisement - Advertisement - Onlykashmir.in News Desk The Jammu and Kashmir Government, led by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, has accorded administrative approval for two major parking infrastructure projects in Jammu city at a combined estimated cost of ₹49.34 crore, a move aimed at easing the persistent traffic congestion that has become a familiar challenge in the winter capital’s busier commercial areas. The approved projects include a Parking-cum-Commercial Complex at Parade and a Multilevel Car Parking facility at SMGS Hospital, two locations that have long struggled with inadequate parking capacity relative to the volume of vehicular traffic and footfall they see on a daily basis. Officials said the projects are intended to provide modern, organised parking facilities at these key locations, easing congestion and improving overall traffic management in the city. The new facilities are also expected to promote better utilisation of available urban space and support planned, sustainable urban development, an approach the government has increasingly emphasised as Jammu continues to grow and its existing infrastructure comes under greater strain. Officials added that the parking infrastructure will offer greater convenience to commuters, visitors and residents alike, particularly in areas that routinely witness heavy vehicular movement and acute parking pressure during peak hours.
